# Postgres type mapping

<!-- generated by scripts/gen-types-doc.py from rowx._core.postgres.type_table(); do not edit by hand -->

This page is generated from the type table in `crates/rowx-postgres/src/types.rs`, the single source of truth for the
runtime codecs and for `rowx check`. Regenerate it with `uv run python scripts/gen-types-doc.py`.

- **Result type** is the Python type a column decodes to, and the leaf your row type must use.
- **Accepted parameters** are the Python types that can be interpolated into a parameter of that type. `None` (SQL
  NULL) is accepted for every parameter.
- **Encoding** is the wire format used to send a parameter.

| Type key | Result type | Timezone | Accepted parameters | Encoding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bool` | `bool` |  | `bool` | binary |
| `int2` | `int` |  | `int` | binary |
| `int4` | `int` |  | `int` | binary |
| `int8` | `int` |  | `int` | binary |
| `oid` | `int` |  | `int` | binary |
| `float4` | `float` |  | `float`, `int` | binary |
| `float8` | `float` |  | `float`, `int` | binary |
| `numeric` | `decimal.Decimal` |  | `Decimal`, `int` | text |
| `text` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `varchar` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `bpchar` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `name` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `citext` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `char` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `bytea` | `bytes` |  | `bytes`, `bytearray`, `memoryview` | binary |
| `date` | `datetime.date` |  | `date` | binary |
| `time` | `datetime.time` | naive | `time` | binary |
| `timetz` | `datetime.time` | aware | `time` | text |
| `timestamp` | `datetime.datetime` | naive | `datetime` | binary |
| `timestamptz` | `datetime.datetime` | aware | `datetime` | binary |
| `interval` | `datetime.timedelta`; or `rowx.postgres.Interval` by annotation |  | `timedelta`, `Interval` | binary |
| `uuid` | `uuid.UUID` |  | `UUID`, `str` | binary |
| `inet` | `ipaddress.IPv4Interface \| ipaddress.IPv6Interface` |  | `IPv4Interface`, `IPv6Interface`, `IPv4Address`, `IPv6Address`, `str` | binary |
| `cidr` | `ipaddress.IPv4Network \| ipaddress.IPv6Network` |  | `IPv4Network`, `IPv6Network`, `str` | binary |
| `macaddr` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `macaddr8` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `int4range` | `rowx.postgres.Range[int]` |  | `Range` | binary |
| `int8range` | `rowx.postgres.Range[int]` |  | `Range` | binary |
| `numrange` | `rowx.postgres.Range[decimal.Decimal]` |  | `Range` | text |
| `daterange` | `rowx.postgres.Range[datetime.date]` |  | `Range` | binary |
| `tsrange` | `rowx.postgres.Range[datetime.datetime]` | naive | `Range` | binary |
| `tstzrange` | `rowx.postgres.Range[datetime.datetime]` | aware | `Range` | binary |
| `money` | `rowx.postgres.Money` |  | `Money` | binary |
| `bit` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `varbit` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `json` | any value (`json.loads`) |  | any JSON-serialisable value | text |
| `jsonb` | any value (`json.loads`) |  | any JSON-serialisable value | text |
| `enum` | `str` |  | `str` | text |
| `domain` | base type |  | base type | base type |
| `array` | `list[X]` |  | `list`, `tuple` | binary, or text if an element needs it |
| `void` | `None` |  | none |  |

## Notes

- `bool` is never accepted for an integer parameter, and `datetime` is never accepted for a `date` parameter.
- A `float4`/`float8` parameter takes an `int`, but an `int` above 2^53 loses precision.
- `str` is never treated as a sequence, so it cannot be bound to an array parameter.
- `json` and `jsonb` accept any JSON-serialisable value, always encoded with `json.dumps`. A `str` becomes a JSON
  string; to bind raw JSON text, write `{s}::text::jsonb`.
- Timezone rules are checked when encoding: a naive `datetime` for `timestamptz` (or an aware one for `timestamp`)
  raises `EncodeError`.
- A domain behaves as its base type.
- An array column decodes to `list[X]` (nested lists for multi-dimensional arrays). `list[X]` and `list[X | None]`
  both match, at every nesting level.
- `void` decodes to `None` and is only valid as a tuple element.
- A range decodes to `rowx.postgres.Range[T]`, with `T` the leaf of its subtype, in the server's canonical form (`[1,5]`
  of `int4range` is `[1, 6)`). A `None` bound is an infinite side, and `Range(empty=True)` is the empty range. A
  user-defined range over `int4`, `int8`, `numeric`, `date`, `timestamp` or `timestamptz` decodes like the built-in
  range of that subtype and keeps whatever form its own canonical function gives it.
- `interval` decodes to `datetime.timedelta`, which raises `DecodeError` for a month component or ±infinity. Annotating
  the column `rowx.postgres.Interval` reads it losslessly as `months`, `days` and `microseconds` instead, and ±infinity
  keeps the server's sentinel fields (the maximum or minimum of each). A parameter takes either class.
- `money` decodes to `rowx.postgres.Money(minor_units)`, the int8 the server sends. rowx holds no scale, because
  `lc_monetary` can change mid-session; `Money.to_decimal(scale)` takes it explicitly. To read the formatted text, cast
  the column to `text`.
- `bit` and `varbit` decode to a `str` of `0` and `1`. A `bit(n)` parameter of any other length is rejected by the
  server.
- Any type not listed here is `unsupported-type` in the checker and raises `DecodeError` at runtime (for example
  multiranges, composites and `xml`).

## Differences from psycopg

Decoding the same server value with rowx and with psycopg gives equal results, except for these cases. A test asserts
that this list matches the one it checks.

- `timestamptz`: rowx always returns a UTC-aware value, while psycopg uses the session `TimeZone`; the instants are
  equal.
- `float4`: rowx widens the exact 32-bit value to a `float`, while psycopg parses the shortest decimal text; the values
  are equal after rounding to 32 bits.
- `char`: A non-ASCII `"char"` is cut to one byte by the server, which is not valid UTF-8, so rowx raises `DecodeError`.
- `interval`: An interval with a month or year part raises `DecodeError` unless the annotation is
  `rowx.postgres.Interval`, while psycopg approximates a month as 30 days.
- `date`: An infinite date raises `DecodeError`, while psycopg raises its own `DataError`.
- `timestamp`: An infinite timestamp raises `DecodeError`, while psycopg raises its own `DataError`.
- `void`: `void` decodes to `None`, while psycopg returns an empty string.
- `inet`: rowx always returns an interface, even for a full-width mask, while psycopg returns an address for `/32` and
  `/128`; the interface's `ip` is that address.
- `int4range`: rowx returns `rowx.postgres.Range`, while psycopg returns its own `Range`; the bounds are equal.
- `int8range`: rowx returns `rowx.postgres.Range`, while psycopg returns its own `Range`; the bounds are equal.
- `numrange`: rowx returns `rowx.postgres.Range`, while psycopg returns its own `Range`; the bounds are equal.
- `daterange`: rowx returns `rowx.postgres.Range`, while psycopg returns its own `Range`; the bounds are equal, but an
  infinite bound of this subtype raises `DecodeError`, while psycopg raises its own `DataError`.
- `tsrange`: rowx returns `rowx.postgres.Range`, while psycopg returns its own `Range`; the bounds are equal, but an
  infinite bound of this subtype raises `DecodeError`, while psycopg raises its own `DataError`.
- `tstzrange`: rowx returns `rowx.postgres.Range`, while psycopg returns its own `Range`; the bounds are equal as
  instants, but an infinite bound of this subtype raises `DecodeError`, while psycopg raises its own `DataError`.
- `money`: rowx returns `rowx.postgres.Money`, the int8 minor units with no scale, while psycopg returns the text the
  server formats under `lc_monetary`.
